relevance.rationale: Same field as the corpus's volume machinery — hyperbolic manifolds, Gromov/simplicial volume, Thurston's ideal-simplex constant v_n — but the operation it studies is not one QOU performs, and its payload lands in dimensions the corpus does not use. The paper's subject is the 2pi-FILLING of a cusped hyperbolic n-manifold (replacing cusps by partial cones), with the headline application being 4-dimensional homology spheres of positive simplicial volume answering a question of Belegradek. QOU's volume constructions glue along essential tori (LinearJSJVolume.lean axiomatizes Vol(AtomicKnot Z N) = Z*Vol_p + N*Vol_n as JSJ additivity, cited to thurston1978) and work in dimension 3 with cusped complements. In dimension 3 Theorem 1.5 reduces to the classical statement that Dehn filling does not increase volume, which the corpus already has from Thurston; nothing in the n >= 4 content has a QOU consumer. I looked specifically for one — the cusp-geometry probes (em_linking_cusp_geometry_probe.py, deltalambda/pion_radius_and_cusp_volume_gap_probe.py) work with cusp shape and volume, not with fillings or with the Gromov norm of a filled pseudomanifold. Scope note: this is a scope-(a) negative — this document, as read, supplies nothing the corpus can use — not a claim that simplicial-volume methods are excluded from the programme.

proposedActions.rationale: Read in full front matter plus all theorem statements; no named place in the corpus wants Theorem 1.5 or its n >= 4 corollaries, and the dimension-3 shadow of the result is already covered by the existing thurston1978 citation in LinearJSJVolume.lean. Registering a ref() entry with no citation site would create a bib orphan.
